celaleyn:1-1.t: ﴿طه﴾ — Allah knows best what He intends by that.

celaleyn:2-2.t: ﴿مَا أَنْزَلْنَا عَلَيْكَ الْقُرْآنَ﴾ — O Muḥammad — ﴿لِتَشْقَى﴾ — so that you exhaust yourself with what you did after its revelation, by standing long in the night prayer; i.e. lighten things for yourself.

celaleyn:3-3.t: ﴿إِلَّا﴾ — but We sent it down — ﴿تَذْكِرَةً﴾ — as a reminder through it — ﴿لِمَنْ يَخْشَى﴾ — for whoever fears Allah.

celaleyn:4-4.t: ﴿تَنْزِيلًا﴾ — a substitute (badal) for the utterance of its verb that puts it in the accusative — ﴿مِمَّنْ خَلَقَ الْأَرْضَ وَالسَّمَاوَاتِ الْعُلَى﴾ — plural of ʿulyā, like kubrā and kubar. He is

celaleyn:5-5.t: ﴿الرَّحْمَنُ عَلَى الْعَرْشِ﴾ — and in the language it is the throne of the king — ﴿اسْتَوَى﴾ — an istiwāʾ (rising) befitting Him.

celaleyn:6-6.t: ﴿لَهُ مَا فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَمَا فِي الْأَرْضِ وَمَا بَيْنَهُمَا﴾ — of created things — ﴿وَمَا تَحْتَ الثَّرَى﴾ — it is moist soil, and what is meant is the seven earths, because they are beneath it.

celaleyn:7-7.t: ﴿وَإِنْ تَجْهَرْ بِالْقَوْلِ﴾ — in remembrance or supplication, then Allah has no need of saying it aloud — ﴿فَإِنَّهُ يَعْلَمُ السِّرَّ وَأَخْفَى﴾ — than it, i.e. what the soul speaks to itself, and what crosses it without its speaking of it; so do not strain yourself by speaking aloud.

celaleyn:8-8.t: ﴿اللَّهُ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا هُوَ لَهُ الْأَسْمَاءُ الْحُسْنَى﴾ — the ninety-nine mentioned in the ḥadīth; and al-ḥusnā is the feminine of al-aḥsan.

celaleyn:10-10.t: ﴿إِذْ رَأَى نَارًا فَقَالَ لِأَهْلِهِ﴾ — to his wife — ﴿امْكُثُوا﴾ — here; and that was on his journey from Madyan heading for Egypt — ﴿إِنِّي آنَسْتُ﴾ — I have seen — ﴿نَارًا لَعَلِّي آتِيكُمْ مِنْهَا بِقَبَسٍ﴾ — with a flame at the tip of a wick or a stick — ﴿أَوْ أَجِدُ عَلَى النَّارِ هُدًى﴾ — i.e. a guide to show me the way; he had lost it because of the darkness of the night. And he said "perhaps" because he could not be certain of fulfilling the promise.

celaleyn:11-11.t: ﴿فَلَمَّا أَتَاهَا﴾ — and it was a boxthorn tree — ﴿نُودِيَ يَا مُوسَى﴾

celaleyn:12-12.t: ﴿إِنِّي﴾ — with kasra on the hamza, by interpreting "nūdiya" (he was called) as "qīla" (it was said), and with fatḥa on it, with the implied bāʾ — ﴿أَنَا﴾ — a tawkīd (emphasis) of the yāʾ of the speaker — ﴿رَبُّكَ فَاخْلَعْ نَعْلَيْكَ إِنَّكَ بِالْوَادِ الْمُقَدَّسِ﴾ — the purified or the blessed — ﴿طُوًى﴾ — a badal (substitute) or ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition), with tanwīn and without it: fully declinable (maṣrūf) when regarded as a place, and a diptote (ghayr maṣrūf) because of femininity when regarded as a plot of land, together with its being a proper name.

celaleyn:13-13.t: ﴿وَأَنَا اخْتَرْتُكَ﴾ — from among your people — ﴿فَاسْتَمِعْ لِمَا يُوحَى﴾ — to you from Me.

celaleyn:14-14.t: ﴿إِنَّنِي أَنَا اللَّهُ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا أَنَا فَاعْبُدْنِي وَأَقِمِ الصَّلَاةَ لِذِكْرِي﴾ — in it.

celaleyn:15-15.t: ﴿إِنَّ السَّاعَةَ آتِيَةٌ أَكَادُ أُخْفِيهَا﴾ — from people, while its nearness becomes apparent to them through its signs — ﴿لِتُجْزَى﴾ — in it — ﴿كُلُّ نَفْسٍ بِمَا تَسْعَى﴾ — in it, of good or evil.

celaleyn:16-16.t: ﴿فَلَا يَصُدَّنَّكَ﴾ — let him not turn you away — ﴿عَنْهَا﴾ — i.e. from believing in it — ﴿مَنْ لَا يُؤْمِنُ بِهَا وَاتَّبَعَ هَوَاهُ﴾ — in denying it — ﴿فَتَرْدَى﴾ — i.e. so that you perish, if you are turned away from it.

celaleyn:17-17.t: ﴿وَمَا تِلْكَ﴾ — being — ﴿بِيَمِينِكَ يَا مُوسَى﴾ — the interrogative is for affirmation (taqrīr), so that He may base the miracle in it upon that.

celaleyn:18-18.t: ﴿قَالَ هِيَ عَصَايَ أَتَوَكَّأُ﴾ — I lean — ﴿عَلَيْهَا﴾ — when leaping and walking — ﴿وَأَهُشُّ﴾ — I beat the leaves of trees — ﴿بِهَا﴾ — so that they fall — ﴿عَلَى غَنَمِي﴾ — and they eat them — ﴿وَلِيَ فِيهَا مَآرِبُ﴾ — plural of maʾraba, with the rāʾ taking any of the three vowels, i.e. needs — ﴿أُخْرَى﴾ — such as carrying provisions and the water-skin, and driving away vermin. And in the answer he added an explanation of his needs for it.

celaleyn:19-19.t: ﴿قَالَ أَلْقِهَا يَا مُوسَى﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here.]

celaleyn:20-20.t: ﴿فَأَلْقَاهَا فَإِذَا هِيَ حَيَّةٌ﴾ — a huge serpent — ﴿تَسْعَى﴾ — moving on its belly quickly, like the quickness of the small snake called al-jānn, by which it is described in another verse.

celaleyn:21-21.t: ﴿قَالَ خُذْهَا وَلَا تَخَفْ﴾ — of it — ﴿سَنُعِيدُهَا سِيرَتَهَا﴾ — accusative by removal of the preposition (manṣūb bi-nazʿ al-khāfiḍ), i.e. to its state — ﴿الْأُولَى﴾ — so he put his hand in its mouth and it turned back into a staff, and it became clear that the place where he put it in was the place where he held it, between its two prongs. The master Mūsā was shown that so that he would not be alarmed when it turned into a serpent before Pharaoh.

celaleyn:22-22.t: ﴿وَاضْمُمْ يَدَكَ﴾ — the right, meaning the palm — ﴿إِلَى جَنَاحِكَ﴾ — i.e. your left side, under the upper arm up to the armpit, and bring it out — ﴿تَخْرُجْ﴾ — contrary to the brownness it had — ﴿بَيْضَاءَ مِنْ غَيْرِ سُوءٍ﴾ — i.e. leprosy, shining like the rays of the sun, dazzling the sight — ﴿آيَةً أُخْرَى﴾ — it and "bayḍāʾ" are two ḥāls (circumstantials) from the pronoun of "takhruj".

celaleyn:23-23.t: ﴿لِنُرِيَكَ﴾ — by it, when you do that to make it appear — ﴿مِنْ آيَاتِنَا﴾ — the sign — ﴿الْكُبْرَى﴾ — i.e. the greatest, of your messengership. And when he wanted it to return to its first state, he pressed it to his side, as mentioned before, and brought it out.

celaleyn:24-24.t: ﴿اذْهَبْ﴾ — as a messenger — ﴿إِلَى فِرْعَوْنَ﴾ — and those with him. ﴿إِنَّهُ طَغَى﴾ — he has exceeded the limit in his disbelief, to the point of claiming divinity.

celaleyn:25-25.t: ﴿قَالَ رَبِّ اشْرَحْ لِي صَدْرِي﴾ — widen it to bear the message.

celaleyn:26-26.t: ﴿وَيَسِّرْ﴾ — make easy — ﴿لِي أَمْرِي﴾ — so that I may convey it.

celaleyn:27-27.t: ﴿وَاحْلُلْ عُقْدَةً مِنْ لِسَانِي﴾ — which arose from its being burnt by a live coal he put in his mouth when he was small.

celaleyn:28-28.t: ﴿يَفْقَهُوا﴾ — so that they understand — ﴿قَوْلِي﴾ — when conveying the message.

celaleyn:29-29.t: ﴿وَاجْعَلْ لِي وَزِيرًا﴾ — a helper in it — ﴿مِنْ أَهْلِي﴾

celaleyn:30-30.t: ﴿هَارُونَ﴾ — a second mafʿūl bihi (direct object) — ﴿أَخِي﴾ — ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition).

celaleyn:32-32.t: ﴿وَأَشْرِكْهُ فِي أَمْرِي﴾ — i.e. the message. The two verbs are [read] in the imperative form and in the jussive (majzūm) imperfect form, and it is the response to the request (jawāb al-ṭalab).

celaleyn:35-35.t: ﴿إِنَّكَ كُنْتَ بِنَا بَصِيرًا﴾ — knowing, so You bestowed the message as a favour.

celaleyn:36-36.t: ﴿قَالَ قَدْ أُوتِيتَ سُؤْلَكَ يَا مُوسَى﴾ — as a favour to you.

celaleyn:37-37.t: ﴿وَلَقَدْ مَنَنَّا عَلَيْكَ مَرَّةً أُخْرَى﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here.]

celaleyn:38-38.t: ﴿إِذْ﴾ — causal (li-l-taʿlīl) — ﴿أَوْحَيْنَا إِلَى أُمِّكَ﴾ — in a dream or by inspiration, when she gave birth to you and feared that Pharaoh would kill you among those being born — ﴿مَا يُوحَى﴾ — concerning you; and there is substituted (badal) from it:

celaleyn:39-39.t: ﴿أَنِ اقْذِفِيهِ﴾ — put him — ﴿فِي التَّابُوتِ فَاقْذِفِيهِ﴾ — with the chest — ﴿فِي الْيَمِّ﴾ — the river Nile — ﴿فَلْيُلْقِهِ الْيَمُّ بِالسَّاحِلِ﴾ — i.e. its bank; and the imperative has the meaning of a statement — ﴿يَأْخُذْهُ عَدُوٌّ لِي وَعَدُوٌّ لَهُ﴾ — and he is Pharaoh. ﴿وَأَلْقَيْتُ﴾ — after they took you — ﴿عَلَيْكَ مَحَبَّةً مِنِّي﴾ — so that you would be loved among people; so Pharaoh loved you, and everyone who saw you — ﴿وَلِتُصْنَعَ عَلَى عَيْنِي﴾ — be brought up under My care and protection of you.

celaleyn:40-40.t: ﴿إِذْ﴾ — causal — ﴿تَمْشِي أُخْتُكَ﴾ — Maryam, to find out news of you, when they had brought wet-nurses and you would not accept the breast of any one of them — ﴿فَتَقُولُ هَلْ أَدُلُّكُمْ عَلَى مَنْ يَكْفُلُهُ﴾ — and she was answered, so she brought his mother and he accepted her breast — ﴿فَرَجَعْنَاكَ إِلَى أُمِّكَ كَيْ تَقَرَّ عَيْنُهَا﴾ — at meeting you — ﴿وَلَا تَحْزَنَ﴾ — then. ﴿وَقَتَلْتَ نَفْسًا﴾ — he is the Copt in Egypt, and you were distressed at having killed him, on account of Pharaoh — ﴿فَنَجَّيْنَاكَ مِنَ الْغَمِّ وَفَتَنَّاكَ فُتُونًا﴾ — We tested you by casting you into other than that and delivered you from it — ﴿فَلَبِثْتَ سِنِينَ﴾ — ten — ﴿فِي أَهْلِ مَدْيَنَ﴾ — after you came to it from Egypt, with Shuʿayb the Prophet, and after you married his daughter — ﴿ثُمَّ جِئْتَ عَلَى قَدَرٍ﴾ — in My knowledge, for the message, and that is at forty years of your age — ﴿يَا مُوسَى﴾.

celaleyn:41-41.t: ﴿وَاصْطَنَعْتُكَ﴾ — I chose you — ﴿لِنَفْسِي﴾ — for the message.

celaleyn:42-42.t: ﴿اذْهَبْ أَنْتَ وَأَخُوكَ﴾ — to the people — ﴿بِآيَاتِي﴾ — the nine — ﴿وَلَا تَنِيَا﴾ — do not slacken — ﴿فِي ذِكْرِي﴾ — with glorification and other than it.

celaleyn:43-43.t: ﴿اذْهَبَا إِلَى فِرْعَوْنَ إِنَّهُ طَغَى﴾ — by his claiming lordship.

celaleyn:44-44.t: ﴿فَقُولَا لَهُ قَوْلًا لَيِّنًا﴾ — about his turning back from that — ﴿لَعَلَّهُ يَتَذَكَّرُ﴾ — take admonition — ﴿أَوْ يَخْشَى﴾ — Allah, and turn back. The hope is relative to the two of them, since He the Exalted knew that he would not turn back.

celaleyn:45-45.t: ﴿قَالَا رَبَّنَا إِنَّنَا نَخَافُ أَنْ يَفْرُطَ عَلَيْنَا﴾ — i.e. hasten to punish — ﴿أَوْ أَنْ يَطْغَى﴾ — against us, i.e. behave arrogantly.

celaleyn:46-46.t: ﴿قَالَ لَا تَخَافَا إِنَّنِي مَعَكُمَا﴾ — with My help — ﴿أَسْمَعُ﴾ — what he says — ﴿وَأَرَى﴾ — what he does.

celaleyn:47-47.t: ﴿فَأْتِيَاهُ فَقُولَا إِنَّا رَسُولَا رَبِّكَ فَأَرْسِلْ مَعَنَا بَنِي إِسْرَائِيلَ﴾ — to Syria — ﴿وَلَا تُعَذِّبْهُمْ﴾ — i.e. release them from your using them in your arduous labours, such as digging, building and carrying heavy loads. ﴿قَدْ جِئْنَاكَ بِآيَةٍ﴾ — with a proof — ﴿مِنْ رَبِّكَ﴾ — of our truthfulness in the message. ﴿وَالسَّلَامُ عَلَى مَنِ اتَّبَعَ الْهُدَى﴾ — i.e. safety for him from punishment.

celaleyn:48-48.t: ﴿إِنَّا قَدْ أُوحِيَ إِلَيْنَا أَنَّ الْعَذَابَ عَلَى مَنْ كَذَّبَ﴾ — what we have brought — ﴿وَتَوَلَّى﴾ — turned away from it. So they came to him and said all that has been mentioned.

celaleyn:49-49.t: ﴿قَالَ فَمَنْ رَبُّكُمَا يَا مُوسَى﴾ — he confined [the address] to him because he is the principal, and in order to humiliate him (li-idhlālihi) by [reminding him of] the upbringing. [Translator's note: the text reads «لِإِذْلَالِهِ» "to humiliate him"; the commonly transmitted reading is «لِإِدْلَالِهِ» "because he presumed upon him", on account of having raised him.]

celaleyn:50-50.t: ﴿قَالَ رَبُّنَا الَّذِي أَعْطَى كُلَّ شَيْءٍ﴾ — of creation — ﴿خَلْقَهُ﴾ — the form it has, by which it is distinguished from others — ﴿ثُمَّ هَدَى﴾ — the animals among it, to their food, their drink, their mating and other than that.

celaleyn:51-51.t: ﴿قَالَ﴾ — Pharaoh — ﴿فَمَا بَالُ﴾ — what is the state of — ﴿الْقُرُونِ﴾ — the nations — ﴿الْأُولَى﴾ — such as the people of Nūḥ, Hūd, Lūṭ and Ṣāliḥ, in their worship of idols?

celaleyn:52-52.t: ﴿قَالَ﴾ — Mūsā — ﴿عِلْمُهَا﴾ — i.e. the knowledge of their state is preserved — ﴿عِنْدَ رَبِّي فِي كِتَابٍ﴾ — it is the Preserved Tablet; He will requite them for it on the Day of Resurrection. ﴿لَا يَضِلُّ﴾ — is not absent — ﴿رَبِّي﴾ — from anything — ﴿وَلَا يَنْسَى﴾ — my Lord does not forget anything. He is

celaleyn:53-53.t: ﴿الَّذِي جَعَلَ لَكُمْ﴾ — among the whole of creation — ﴿الْأَرْضَ مَهْدًا﴾ — a bed — ﴿وَسَلَكَ﴾ — made easy — ﴿لَكُمْ فِيهَا سُبُلًا﴾ — roads — ﴿وَأَنْزَلَ مِنَ السَّمَاءِ مَاءً﴾ — rain. The Exalted said, completing what Mūsā described Him with, and addressing the people of Mecca: ﴿فَأَخْرَجْنَا بِهِ أَزْوَاجًا﴾ — kinds — ﴿مِنْ نَبَاتٍ شَتَّى﴾ — an adjective (ṣifa) of "azwājan", i.e. differing in colours, tastes and other things; and shattā is the plural of shatīt, like marīḍ and marḍā, from "shatta al-amr" (the matter became scattered), i.e. it became dispersed.

celaleyn:54-54.t: ﴿كُلُوا﴾ — of it — ﴿وَارْعَوْا أَنْعَامَكُمْ﴾ — in it; plural of naʿam, which are camels, cattle and sheep. One says "raʿat al-anʿām" (the livestock grazed) and "raʿaytuhā" (I grazed them). The imperative is for permission and as a reminder of the blessing, and the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun of "akhrajnā", i.e. permitting you to eat and to graze livestock. ﴿إِنَّ فِي ذَلِكَ﴾ — what is mentioned here — ﴿لَآيَاتٍ﴾ — lessons — ﴿لِأُولِي النُّهَى﴾ — for those possessed of intellects; plural of nuhya, like ghurfa and ghuraf. The intellect is called by it because it forbids (yanhā) its possessor from committing vile acts.

celaleyn:55-55.t: ﴿مِنْهَا﴾ — i.e. from the earth — ﴿خَلَقْنَاكُمْ﴾ — by creating your father Ādam from it — ﴿وَفِيهَا نُعِيدُكُمْ﴾ — buried after death — ﴿وَمِنْهَا نُخْرِجُكُمْ﴾ — at the resurrection — ﴿تَارَةً﴾ — a time — ﴿أُخْرَى﴾ — just as We brought you out at the beginning of your creation.

celaleyn:56-56.t: ﴿وَلَقَدْ أَرَيْنَاهُ﴾ — i.e. We made Pharaoh see — ﴿آيَاتِنَا كُلَّهَا﴾ — the nine — ﴿فَكَذَّبَ﴾ — them, and claimed that they were sorcery — ﴿وَأَبَى﴾ — to affirm the oneness of Allah the Exalted.

celaleyn:57-57.t: ﴿قَالَ أَجِئْتَنَا لِتُخْرِجَنَا مِنْ أَرْضِنَا﴾ — Egypt, so that sovereignty in it would be yours — ﴿بِسِحْرِكَ يَا مُوسَى﴾

celaleyn:58-58.t: ﴿فَلَنَأْتِيَنَّكَ بِسِحْرٍ مِثْلِهِ﴾ — to counter it — ﴿فَاجْعَلْ بَيْنَنَا وَبَيْنَكَ مَوْعِدًا﴾ — for that — ﴿لَا نُخْلِفُهُ نَحْنُ وَلَا أَنْتَ مَكَانًا﴾ — accusative by removal of the preposition (manṣūb bi-nazʿ al-khāfiḍ) "fī" — ﴿سِوًى﴾ — with kasra on its first letter, and with ḍamma [سُوًى], i.e. a middle point to which the distance is equal for one coming from either side.

celaleyn:59-59.t: ﴿قَالَ﴾ — Mūsā — ﴿مَوْعِدُكُمْ يَوْمُ الزِّينَةِ﴾ — a feast day of theirs on which they adorned themselves and gathered — ﴿وَأَنْ يُحْشَرَ النَّاسُ﴾ — the people of Egypt be gathered — ﴿ضُحًى﴾ — at its forenoon, to watch what would take place.

celaleyn:60-60.t: ﴿فَتَوَلَّى فِرْعَوْنُ﴾ — turned back — ﴿فَجَمَعَ كَيْدَهُ﴾ — i.e. the people of his scheme, from among the sorcerers — ﴿ثُمَّ أَتَى﴾ — with them, at the appointed time.

celaleyn:61-61.t: ﴿قَالَ لَهُمْ مُوسَى﴾ — and they were seventy-two, each with a rope and a staff — ﴿وَيْلَكُمْ﴾ — i.e. may Allah make woe cling to you — ﴿لَا تَفْتَرُوا عَلَى اللَّهِ كَذِبًا﴾ — by associating anyone with Him — ﴿فَيُسْحِتَكُمْ﴾ — with ḍamma on the yāʾ and kasra on the ḥāʾ, and with fatḥa on both, i.e. He will destroy you — ﴿بِعَذَابٍ﴾ — from Him. ﴿وَقَدْ خَابَ﴾ — has lost — ﴿مَنِ افْتَرَى﴾ — lied against Allah.

celaleyn:62-62.t: ﴿فَتَنَازَعُوا أَمْرَهُمْ بَيْنَهُمْ﴾ — concerning Mūsā and his brother — ﴿وَأَسَرُّوا النَّجْوَى﴾ — i.e. the talk among them about the two of them.

celaleyn:63-63.t: ﴿قَالُوا﴾ — to themselves — ﴿إِنَّ هَذَيْنِ﴾ — this is Abū ʿAmr's [reading], and for the others [هَذَانِ], which agrees with the dialect of those who use the alif in the dual in all three of its cases — ﴿لَسَاحِرَانِ يُرِيدَانِ أَنْ يُخْرِجَاكُمْ مِنْ أَرْضِكُمْ بِسِحْرِهِمَا وَيَذْهَبَا بِطَرِيقَتِكُمُ الْمُثْلَى﴾ — feminine of amthal, meaning "most noble", i.e. with your nobles, by their inclining to the two of them because of their victory.

celaleyn:64-64.t: ﴿فَاجْمَعُوا كَيْدَكُمْ﴾ — of sorcery; with the connecting hamza (hamzat waṣl) and fatḥa on the mīm, from "jamaʿa", i.e. "gather together"; and with the disjunctive hamza (hamzat qaṭʿ) and kasra on the mīm [فَأَجْمِعُوا], from "ajmaʿa": "make firm". ﴿ثُمَّ ائْتُوا صَفًّا﴾ — a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. lined up in ranks. ﴿وَقَدْ أَفْلَحَ﴾ — has succeeded — ﴿الْيَوْمَ مَنِ اسْتَعْلَى﴾ — prevailed.

celaleyn:65-65.t: ﴿قَالُوا يَا مُوسَى﴾ — choose — ﴿إِمَّا أَنْ تُلْقِيَ﴾ — your staff, i.e. first — ﴿وَإِمَّا أَنْ نَكُونَ أَوَّلَ مَنْ أَلْقَى﴾ — his staff.

celaleyn:66-66.t: ﴿قَالَ بَلْ أَلْقُوا﴾ — so they threw — ﴿فَإِذَا حِبَالُهُمْ وَعِصِيُّهُمْ﴾ — its original form is ʿuṣuwwun; the two wāws were changed into two yāʾs, and the ʿayn and the ṣād were given kasra — ﴿يُخَيَّلُ إِلَيْهِ مِنْ سِحْرِهِمْ أَنَّهَا﴾ — snakes — ﴿تَسْعَى﴾ — on their bellies.

celaleyn:67-67.t: ﴿فَأَوْجَسَ﴾ — sensed — ﴿فِي نَفْسِهِ خِيفَةً مُوسَى﴾ — i.e. he feared, on account of their sorcery being of the same kind as his miracles, that his matter would become confused for the people and they would not believe in him.

celaleyn:68-68.t: ﴿قُلْنَا﴾ — to him — ﴿لَا تَخَفْ إِنَّكَ أَنْتَ الْأَعْلَى﴾ — over them, by victory.

celaleyn:69-69.t: ﴿وَأَلْقِ مَا فِي يَمِينِكَ﴾ — and it was his staff — ﴿تَلْقَفْ﴾ — it will swallow — ﴿مَا صَنَعُوا إِنَّمَا صَنَعُوا كَيْدُ سَاحِرٍ﴾ — i.e. of its kind — ﴿وَلَا يُفْلِحُ السَّاحِرُ حَيْثُ أَتَى﴾ — with his sorcery. So Mūsā threw his staff, and it swallowed everything they had made.

celaleyn:70-70.t: ﴿فَأُلْقِيَ السَّحَرَةُ سُجَّدًا﴾ — they fell down prostrating to Allah the Exalted. ﴿قَالُوا آمَنَّا بِرَبِّ هَارُونَ وَمُوسَى﴾

celaleyn:71-71.t: ﴿قَالَ﴾ — Pharaoh — ﴿أَآمَنْتُمْ﴾ — with both hamzas pronounced fully, and with the second changed into an alif [آمَنْتُمْ] — ﴿لَهُ قَبْلَ أَنْ آذَنَ﴾ — I — ﴿لَكُمْ إِنَّهُ لَكَبِيرُكُمْ﴾ — your teacher — ﴿الَّذِي عَلَّمَكُمُ السِّحْرَ فَلَأُقَطِّعَنَّ أَيْدِيَكُمْ وَأَرْجُلَكُمْ مِنْ خِلَافٍ﴾ — a ḥāl (circumstantial) meaning "on opposite sides", i.e. the right hands and the left feet — ﴿وَلَأُصَلِّبَنَّكُمْ فِي جُذُوعِ النَّخْلِ﴾ — i.e. on them — ﴿وَلَتَعْلَمُنَّ أَيُّنَا﴾ — meaning himself and the Lord of Mūsā — ﴿أَشَدُّ عَذَابًا وَأَبْقَى﴾ — more lasting, for opposing him.

celaleyn:72-72.t: ﴿قَالُوا لَنْ نُؤْثِرَكَ﴾ — choose you — ﴿عَلَى مَا جَاءَنَا مِنَ الْبَيِّنَاتِ﴾ — which prove Mūsā's truthfulness — ﴿وَالَّذِي فَطَرَنَا﴾ — created us; an oath, or conjoined (maʿṭūf) to "mā". ﴿فَاقْضِ مَا أَنْتَ قَاضٍ﴾ — i.e. do what you have said. ﴿إِنَّمَا تَقْضِي هَذِهِ الْحَيَاةَ الدُّنْيَا﴾ — the accusative is by extension (ʿalā al-ittisāʿ), i.e. in it; and you will be requited for it in the Hereafter.

celaleyn:73-73.t: ﴿إِنَّا آمَنَّا بِرَبِّنَا لِيَغْفِرَ لَنَا خَطَايَانَا﴾ — of associating partners and other things — ﴿وَمَا أَكْرَهْتَنَا عَلَيْهِ مِنَ السِّحْرِ﴾ — in learning and practice, to counter Mūsā. ﴿وَاللَّهُ خَيْرٌ﴾ — than you in reward when obeyed — ﴿وَأَبْقَى﴾ — than you in punishment when disobeyed. The Exalted said:

celaleyn:74-74.t: ﴿إِنَّهُ مَنْ يَأْتِ رَبَّهُ مُجْرِمًا﴾ — a disbeliever, like Pharaoh — ﴿فَإِنَّ لَهُ جَهَنَّمَ لَا يَمُوتُ فِيهَا﴾ — so as to find rest — ﴿وَلَا يَحْيَى﴾ — a life that benefits him.

celaleyn:75-75.t: ﴿وَمَنْ يَأْتِهِ مُؤْمِنًا قَدْ عَمِلَ الصَّالِحَاتِ﴾ — the obligatory and the supererogatory — ﴿فَأُولَئِكَ لَهُمُ الدَّرَجَاتُ الْعُلَى﴾ — plural of ʿulyā, feminine of aʿlā.

celaleyn:76-76.t: ﴿جَنَّاتُ عَدْنٍ﴾ — i.e. of residence; an explication (bayān) of it — ﴿تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهَا الْأَنْهَارُ خَالِدِينَ فِيهَا وَذَلِكَ جَزَاءُ مَنْ تَزَكَّى﴾ — purified himself of sins.

celaleyn:77-77.t: ﴿وَلَقَدْ أَوْحَيْنَا إِلَى مُوسَى أَنْ أَسْرِ بِعِبَادِي﴾ — with the disjunctive hamza (hamzat qaṭʿ), from asrā, and with the connecting hamza (hamzat waṣl) and kasra on the nūn, from sarā — two dialects; i.e. travel with them by night from the land of Egypt — ﴿فَاضْرِبْ﴾ — make — ﴿لَهُمْ﴾ — by striking with your staff — ﴿طَرِيقًا فِي الْبَحْرِ يَبَسًا﴾ — i.e. dry. So he carried out what he was commanded, and Allah dried the ground, and they passed through it. ﴿لَا تَخَافُ دَرَكًا﴾ — i.e. that Pharaoh would overtake you — ﴿وَلَا تَخْشَى﴾ — drowning.

celaleyn:78-78.t: ﴿فَأَتْبَعَهُمْ فِرْعَوْنُ بِجُنُودِهِ﴾ — and he was with them — ﴿فَغَشِيَهُمْ مِنَ الْيَمِّ﴾ — i.e. the sea — ﴿مَا غَشِيَهُمْ﴾ — and drowned them.

celaleyn:79-79.t: ﴿وَأَضَلَّ فِرْعَوْنُ قَوْمَهُ﴾ — by calling them to worship him — ﴿وَمَا هَدَى﴾ — rather he cast them into destruction, contrary to his saying {وَمَا أَهْدِيكُمْ إِلَّا سَبِيلَ الرَّشَادِ}.

celaleyn:80-80.t: ﴿يَا بَنِي إِسْرَائِيلَ قَدْ أَنْجَيْنَاكُمْ مِنْ عَدُوِّكُمْ﴾ — Pharaoh, by drowning him — ﴿وَوَاعَدْنَاكُمْ جَانِبَ الطُّورِ الْأَيْمَنَ﴾ — so We would give Mūsā the Torah to act upon — ﴿وَنَزَّلْنَا عَلَيْكُمُ الْمَنَّ وَالسَّلْوَى﴾ — they are taranjabīn (manna) and the bird al-sumānā (quail), with the mīm without shadda and with the short ending. Those addressed are the Jews present in the time of the Prophet ﷺ; they were addressed with what Allah bestowed upon their ancestors in the time of the Prophet Mūsā, as a preparation for His words, the Exalted, to them:

celaleyn:81-81.t: ﴿كُلُوا مِنْ طَيِّبَاتِ مَا رَزَقْنَاكُمْ﴾ — i.e. what has been bestowed upon you — ﴿وَلَا تَطْغَوْا فِيهِ﴾ — by being ungrateful for the blessing of it — ﴿فَيَحِلَّ عَلَيْكُمْ غَضَبِي﴾ — with kasra on the ḥāʾ, i.e. becomes due, and with ḍamma on it, i.e. descends — ﴿وَمَنْ يَحْلِلْ عَلَيْهِ غَضَبِي﴾ — with kasra on the lām and with ḍamma — ﴿فَقَدْ هَوَى﴾ — has fallen into the Fire.

celaleyn:82-82.t: ﴿وَإِنِّي لَغَفَّارٌ لِمَنْ تَابَ﴾ — from idolatry (shirk) — ﴿وَآمَنَ﴾ — affirmed the oneness of Allah — ﴿وَعَمِلَ صَالِحًا﴾ — it applies to the obligatory and the supererogatory — ﴿ثُمَّ اهْتَدَى﴾ — by persisting in what has been mentioned until his death.

celaleyn:83-83.t: ﴿وَمَا أَعْجَلَكَ عَنْ قَوْمِكَ﴾ — in coming to the appointment for receiving the Torah — ﴿يَا مُوسَى﴾

celaleyn:84-84.t: ﴿قَالَ هُمْ أُولَاءِ﴾ — i.e. near me, coming — ﴿عَلَى أَثَرِي وَعَجِلْتُ إِلَيْكَ رَبِّ لِتَرْضَى﴾ — with me, i.e. in addition to Your good pleasure. Before the answer he offered an excuse according to what he supposed, and what he supposed did not hold, because of what [follows]: [Translator's note: the text ends with «لِمَا» "because of what", which runs on into the next ayah.]

celaleyn:85-85.t: ﴿قَالَ﴾ — the Exalted — ﴿فَإِنَّا قَدْ فَتَنَّا قَوْمَكَ مِنْ بَعْدِكَ﴾ — i.e. after your parting from them — ﴿وَأَضَلَّهُمُ السَّامِرِيُّ﴾ — so they worshipped the calf.

celaleyn:86-86.t: ﴿فَرَجَعَ مُوسَى إِلَى قَوْمِهِ غَضْبَانَ﴾ — on account of them — ﴿أَسِفًا﴾ — intensely grieved. ﴿قَالَ يَا قَوْمِ أَلَمْ يَعِدْكُمْ رَبُّكُمْ وَعْدًا حَسَنًا﴾ — i.e. a true one, that He would give you the Torah? ﴿أَفَطَالَ عَلَيْكُمُ الْعَهْدُ﴾ — the period of my separation from you — ﴿أَمْ أَرَدْتُمْ أَنْ يَحِلَّ﴾ — become due — ﴿عَلَيْكُمْ غَضَبٌ مِنْ رَبِّكُمْ﴾ — through your worship of the calf — ﴿فَأَخْلَفْتُمْ مَوْعِدِي﴾ — and abandoned coming after me?

celaleyn:87-87.t: ﴿قَالُوا مَا أَخْلَفْنَا مَوْعِدَكَ بِمَلْكِنَا﴾ — with the mīm taking any of the three vowels, i.e. by our own power or choice — ﴿وَلَكِنَّا حَمَلْنَا﴾ — with fatḥa on the ḥāʾ and without shadda, and with ḍamma on it and kasra on the mīm with shadda [حُمِّلْنَا] — ﴿أَوْزَارًا﴾ — loads — ﴿مِنْ زِينَةِ الْقَوْمِ﴾ — i.e. the jewellery of Pharaoh's people, which the Children of Israel had borrowed from them on the pretext of a wedding, and it remained with them — ﴿فَقَذَفْنَاهَا﴾ — we threw it into the fire, at the command of al-Sāmirī — ﴿فَكَذَلِكَ﴾ — just as we threw — ﴿أَلْقَى السَّامِرِيُّ﴾ — what he had with him of their jewellery and of the dust he had taken from the hoofprint of Jibrīl's horse, in the way that will come.

celaleyn:88-88.t: ﴿فَأَخْرَجَ لَهُمْ عِجْلًا﴾ — which he cast from the jewellery — ﴿جَسَدًا﴾ — flesh and blood — ﴿لَهُ خُوَارٌ﴾ — i.e. an audible sound; i.e. it was transformed thus because of the dust, whose effect is life in whatever it is placed in; and he placed it in its mouth after casting it. ﴿فَقَالُوا﴾ — i.e. al-Sāmirī and his followers — ﴿هَذَا إِلَهُكُمْ وَإِلَهُ مُوسَى فَنَسِيَ﴾ — Mūsā forgot his Lord here and went off seeking Him. The Exalted said:

celaleyn:89-89.t: ﴿أَفَلَا يَرَوْنَ أَلَّا﴾ — "an" is lightened from the heavy one (mukhaffafa min al-thaqīla), and its noun is omitted, i.e. "that it does not" — ﴿يَرْجِعُ﴾ — the calf — ﴿إِلَيْهِمْ قَوْلًا﴾ — i.e. does not return an answer to them — ﴿وَلَا يَمْلِكُ لَهُمْ ضَرًّا﴾ — i.e. to ward it off — ﴿وَلَا نَفْعًا﴾ — i.e. to bring it? I.e. so how can it be taken as a god?

celaleyn:90-90.t: ﴿وَلَقَدْ قَالَ لَهُمْ هَارُونُ مِنْ قَبْلُ﴾ — i.e. before Mūsā returned — ﴿يَا قَوْمِ إِنَّمَا فُتِنْتُمْ بِهِ وَإِنَّ رَبَّكُمُ الرَّحْمَنُ فَاتَّبِعُونِي﴾ — in worshipping Him — ﴿وَأَطِيعُوا أَمْرِي﴾ — in it.

celaleyn:91-91.t: ﴿قَالُوا لَنْ نَبْرَحَ﴾ — we will not cease — ﴿عَلَيْهِ عَاكِفِينَ﴾ — persisting in worshipping it — ﴿حَتَّى يَرْجِعَ إِلَيْنَا مُوسَى﴾

celaleyn:92-92.t: ﴿قَالَ﴾ — Mūsā, after his return — ﴿يَا هَارُونُ مَا مَنَعَكَ إِذْ رَأَيْتَهُمْ ضَلُّوا﴾ — by worshipping it,

celaleyn:93-93.t: ﴿أَلَّا تَتَّبِعَنِ﴾ — "lā" is redundant (zāʾida). ﴿أَفَعَصَيْتَ أَمْرِي﴾ — by your remaining among those who worship other than Allah the Exalted?

celaleyn:94-94.t: ﴿قَالَ﴾ — Hārūn — ﴿يَا ابْنَ أُمِّ﴾ — with kasra on the mīm and with fatḥa on it [أُمَّ]; he meant "my mother", and mentioning her is more apt to soften his heart — ﴿لَا تَأْخُذْ بِلِحْيَتِي﴾ — he had seized it with his left hand — ﴿وَلَا بِرَأْسِي﴾ — he had seized his hair with his right hand, in anger. ﴿إِنِّي خَشِيتُ﴾ — if I had followed you, and a group of those who had not worshipped the calf would inevitably have followed me — ﴿أَنْ تَقُولَ فَرَّقْتَ بَيْنَ بَنِي إِسْرَائِيلَ﴾ — and be angry with me — ﴿وَلَمْ تَرْقُبْ﴾ — wait for — ﴿قَوْلِي﴾ — about what I saw [fit] in that.

celaleyn:95-95.t: ﴿قَالَ فَمَا خَطْبُكَ﴾ — your affair, which led to what you did — ﴿يَا سَامِرِيُّ﴾

celaleyn:96-96.t: ﴿قَالَ بَصُرْتُ بِمَا لَمْ يَبْصُرُوا بِهِ﴾ — with yāʾ and with tāʾ, i.e. I knew what they did not know — ﴿فَقَبَضْتُ قَبْضَةً مِنْ﴾ — the dust of — ﴿أَثَرِ﴾ — the hoof of the horse of — ﴿الرَّسُولِ﴾ — Jibrīl — ﴿فَنَبَذْتُهَا﴾ — I threw it into the form of the cast calf. ﴿وَكَذَلِكَ سَوَّلَتْ﴾ — made attractive — ﴿لِي نَفْسِي﴾ — and it was cast into it that I should take a handful of the dust mentioned and throw it on what has no soul, and it would come to have a soul. And I saw that your people had asked you to make a god for them, so my soul suggested to me that this calf should be their god.

celaleyn:97-97.t: ﴿قَالَ﴾ — Mūsā to him — ﴿فَاذْهَبْ﴾ — from among us — ﴿فَإِنَّ لَكَ فِي الْحَيَاةِ﴾ — i.e. for the duration of your life — ﴿أَنْ تَقُولَ﴾ — to whomever you see — ﴿لَا مِسَاسَ﴾ — i.e. do not come near me. So he used to wander in the wilderness, and whenever he touched anyone or anyone touched him, they both came down with fever. ﴿وَإِنَّ لَكَ مَوْعِدًا﴾ — for your punishment — ﴿لَنْ تُخْلِفَهُ﴾ — with kasra on the lām, i.e. you will not be absent from it, and with fatḥa on it [تُخْلَفَهُ], i.e. rather you will be raised up to it. ﴿وَانْظُرْ إِلَى إِلَهِكَ الَّذِي ظَلْتَ﴾ — its original form is ẓalilta, with two lāms, the first of which has kasra; it was dropped for lightness; i.e. you continued — ﴿عَلَيْهِ عَاكِفًا﴾ — i.e. remaining in worship of it — ﴿لَنُحَرِّقَنَّهُ﴾ — with fire — ﴿ثُمَّ لَنَنْسِفَنَّهُ فِي الْيَمِّ نَسْفًا﴾ — We will scatter it in the air over the sea. And Mūsā, after slaughtering it, did what he mentioned.

celaleyn:98-98.t: ﴿إِنَّمَا إِلَهُكُمُ اللَّهُ الَّذِي لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا هُوَ وَسِعَ كُلَّ شَيْءٍ عِلْمًا﴾ — a tamyīz (specification) converted from the fāʿil (agent), i.e. His knowledge encompasses everything.

celaleyn:99-99.t: ﴿كَذَلِكَ﴾ — i.e. just as We have narrated this story to you, O Muḥammad — ﴿نَقُصُّ عَلَيْكَ مِنْ أَنْبَاءِ﴾ — the reports of — ﴿مَا قَدْ سَبَقَ﴾ — of the nations — ﴿وَقَدْ آتَيْنَاكَ﴾ — We have given you — ﴿مِنْ لَدُنَّا﴾ — from Us — ﴿ذِكْرًا﴾ — a Quran.

celaleyn:100-100.t: ﴿مَنْ أَعْرَضَ عَنْهُ﴾ — and did not believe in it — ﴿فَإِنَّهُ يَحْمِلُ يَوْمَ الْقِيَمَةِ وِزْرًا﴾ — a heavy load of sin,

celaleyn:101-101.t: ﴿خَالِدِينَ فِيهِ﴾ — i.e. in the punishment of the burden. ﴿وَسَاءَ لَهُمْ يَوْمَ الْقِيَمَةِ حِمْلًا﴾ — a tamyīz (specification) explaining the pronoun in "sāʾa", and the one specified for blame (al-makhṣūṣ bi-l-dhamm) is omitted, its implied form being "their burden"; and the lām is for clarification (li-l-bayān). And there is substituted (badal) from "yawm al-qiyāma":

celaleyn:102-102.t: ﴿يَوْمَ يُنْفَخُ فِي الصُّورِ﴾ — the horn — the second blowing — ﴿وَنَحْشُرُ الْمُجْرِمِينَ﴾ — the disbelievers — ﴿يَوْمَئِذٍ زُرْقًا﴾ — their eyes [blue], along with the blackness of their faces.

celaleyn:103-103.t: ﴿يَتَخَافَتُونَ بَيْنَهُمْ﴾ — whispering to one another: ﴿إِنْ﴾ — "not" — ﴿لَبِثْتُمْ﴾ — in the world — ﴿إِلَّا عَشْرًا﴾ — nights, with their days.

celaleyn:104-104.t: ﴿نَحْنُ أَعْلَمُ بِمَا يَقُولُونَ﴾ — about that, i.e. it is not as they said — ﴿إِذْ يَقُولُ أَمْثَلُهُمْ﴾ — the most balanced of them — ﴿طَرِيقَةً﴾ — in it: ﴿إِنْ لَبِثْتُمْ إِلَّا يَوْمًا﴾ — they deem their stay in the world very short because of the terrors of the Hereafter that they witness.

celaleyn:105-105.t: ﴿وَيَسْأَلُونَكَ عَنِ الْجِبَالِ﴾ — how they will be on the Day of Resurrection — ﴿فَقُلْ﴾ — to them — ﴿يَنْسِفُهَا رَبِّي نَسْفًا﴾ — by crumbling them like flowing sand, then it is blown away by the wind.

celaleyn:107-107.t: ﴿لَا تَرَى فِيهَا عِوَجًا﴾ — a depression — ﴿وَلَا أَمْتًا﴾ — an elevation.

celaleyn:108-108.t: ﴿يَوْمَئِذٍ﴾ — i.e. on the day when the mountains are blown away — ﴿يَتَّبِعُونَ﴾ — i.e. people, after rising from the graves — ﴿الدَّاعِيَ﴾ — to the place of gathering, with his voice; and he is Isrāfīl, saying: "Come to the presentation before the Most Merciful" — ﴿لَا عِوَجَ لَهُ﴾ — i.e. to their following him; i.e. they are not able not to follow. ﴿وَخَشَعَتِ﴾ — became still — ﴿الْأَصْوَاتُ لِلرَّحْمَنِ فَلَا تَسْمَعُ إِلَّا هَمْسًا﴾ — the sound of the treading of feet as they move to the place of gathering, like the sound of camels' pads as they walk.

celaleyn:109-109.t: ﴿يَوْمَئِذٍ لَا تَنْفَعُ الشَّفَاعَةُ﴾ — anyone — ﴿إِلَّا مَنْ أَذِنَ لَهُ الرَّحْمَنُ﴾ — that intercession be made for him — ﴿وَرَضِيَ لَهُ قَوْلًا﴾ — by his saying "there is no god but Allah".

celaleyn:110-110.t: ﴿يَعْلَمُ مَا بَيْنَ أَيْدِيهِمْ﴾ — of the affairs of the Hereafter — ﴿وَمَا خَلْفَهُمْ﴾ — of the affairs of this world — ﴿وَلَا يُحِيطُونَ بِهِ عِلْمًا﴾ — they do not know that.

celaleyn:111-111.t: ﴿وَعَنَتِ الْوُجُوهُ﴾ — submitted — ﴿لِلْحَيِّ الْقَيُّومِ﴾ — i.e. Allah. ﴿وَقَدْ خَابَ﴾ — has lost — ﴿مَنْ حَمَلَ ظُلْمًا﴾ — i.e. idolatry (shirk).

celaleyn:112-112.t: ﴿وَمَنْ يَعْمَلْ مِنَ الصَّالِحَاتِ﴾ — acts of obedience — ﴿وَهُوَ مُؤْمِنٌ فَلَا يَخَافُ ظُلْمًا﴾ — through an increase in his bad deeds — ﴿وَلَا هَضْمًا﴾ — through a decrease in his good deeds.

celaleyn:113-113.t: ﴿وَكَذَلِكَ﴾ — conjoined (maʿṭūf) to "kadhālika naquṣṣu", i.e. like the sending down of what has been mentioned — ﴿أَنْزَلْنَاهُ﴾ — i.e. the Quran — ﴿قُرْآنًا عَرَبِيًّا وَصَرَّفْنَا﴾ — We repeated — ﴿فِيهِ مِنَ الْوَعِيدِ لَعَلَّهُمْ يَتَّقُونَ﴾ — idolatry — ﴿أَوْ يُحْدِثُ﴾ — the Quran — ﴿لَهُمْ ذِكْرًا﴾ — of the destruction of the nations that preceded them, so that they take heed.

celaleyn:114-114.t: ﴿فَتَعَالَى اللَّهُ الْمَلِكُ الْحَقُّ﴾ — above what the idolaters say. ﴿وَلَا تَعْجَلْ بِالْقُرْآنِ﴾ — i.e. in reciting it — ﴿مِنْ قَبْلِ أَنْ يُقْضَى إِلَيْكَ وَحْيُهُ﴾ — i.e. before Jibrīl finishes conveying it. ﴿وَقُلْ رَبِّ زِدْنِي عِلْمًا﴾ — i.e. of the Quran; so whenever something of it was sent down to him, his knowledge increased by it.

celaleyn:115-115.t: ﴿وَلَقَدْ عَهِدْنَا إِلَى آدَمَ﴾ — We enjoined him not to eat from the tree — ﴿مِنْ قَبْلُ﴾ — i.e. before his eating from it — ﴿فَنَسِيَ﴾ — he abandoned Our covenant — ﴿وَلَمْ نَجِدْ لَهُ عَزْمًا﴾ — firmness and patience in refraining from what We forbade him.

celaleyn:116-116.t: ﴿وَ﴾ — remember — ﴿إِذْ قُلْنَا لِلْمَلَائِكَةِ اسْجُدُوا لِآدَمَ فَسَجَدُوا إِلَّا إِبْلِيسَ﴾ — and he is the father of the jinn; he used to keep company with the angels and worship Allah with them — ﴿أَبَى﴾ — to prostrate to Ādam; he said, "I am better than him."

celaleyn:117-117.t: ﴿فَقُلْنَا يَا آدَمُ إِنَّ هَذَا عَدُوٌّ لَكَ وَلِزَوْجِكَ﴾ — Ḥawwāʾ, with the long vowel — ﴿فَلَا يُخْرِجَنَّكُمَا مِنَ الْجَنَّةِ فَتَشْقَى﴾ — and toil at ploughing, sowing, reaping, grinding, baking and other than that. He limited it to his toil because the man labours for his wife.

celaleyn:118-118.t: ﴿إِنَّ لَكَ أَلَّا تَجُوعَ فِيهَا وَلَا تَعْرَى﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here.]

celaleyn:119-119.t: ﴿وَأَنَّكَ﴾ — with fatḥa on the hamza and with kasra on it; conjoined to the noun of "inna" and to its clause — ﴿لَا تَظْمَأُ فِيهَا﴾ — become thirsty — ﴿وَلَا تَضْحَى﴾ — the heat of the forenoon sun will not reach you, because there is no sun in Paradise.

celaleyn:120-120.t: ﴿فَوَسْوَسَ إِلَيْهِ الشَّيْطَانُ قَالَ يَا آدَمُ هَلْ أَدُلُّكَ عَلَى شَجَرَةِ الْخُلْدِ﴾ — i.e. the one whoever eats from it lives forever — ﴿وَمُلْكٍ لَا يَبْلَى﴾ — does not perish; and it is a necessary consequence of eternal life.

celaleyn:121-121.t: ﴿فَأَكَلَا﴾ — i.e. Ādam and Ḥawwāʾ — ﴿مِنْهَا فَبَدَتْ لَهُمَا سَوْآتُهُمَا﴾ — i.e. to each of them his own front private part and that of the other, and his rear, became visible; each of them is called sawʾa because its exposure distresses (yasūʾu) its owner — ﴿وَطَفِقَا يَخْصِفَانِ﴾ — they began to stick — ﴿عَلَيْهِمَا مِنْ وَرَقِ الْجَنَّةِ﴾ — to cover themselves with it. ﴿وَعَصَى آدَمُ رَبَّهُ فَغَوَى﴾ — by eating from the tree.

celaleyn:122-122.t: ﴿ثُمَّ اجْتَبَاهُ رَبُّهُ﴾ — brought him near — ﴿فَتَابَ عَلَيْهِ﴾ — accepted his repentance — ﴿وَهَدَى﴾ — i.e. guided him to persevere in repentance.

celaleyn:123-123.t: ﴿قَالَ اهْبِطَا﴾ — i.e. Ādam and Ḥawwāʾ, together with the offspring you contain — ﴿مِنْهَا﴾ — from Paradise — ﴿جَمِيعًا بَعْضُكُمْ﴾ — some of the offspring — ﴿لِبَعْضٍ عَدُوٌّ﴾ — through some of them wronging others. ﴿فَإِمَّا﴾ — in it is the assimilation of the nūn of the conditional "in" into the added "mā" — ﴿يَأْتِيَنَّكُمْ مِنِّي هُدًى فَمَنِ اتَّبَعَ هُدَايَ﴾ — i.e. the Quran — ﴿فَلَا يَضِلُّ﴾ — in this world — ﴿وَلَا يَشْقَى﴾ — in the Hereafter.

celaleyn:124-124.t: ﴿وَمَنْ أَعْرَضَ عَنْ ذِكْرِي﴾ — i.e. the Quran, and did not believe in it — ﴿فَإِنَّ لَهُ مَعِيشَةً ضَنْكًا﴾ — with tanwīn; a maṣdar (verbal noun) meaning "narrow"; and in a ḥadīth it is explained as the punishment of the disbeliever in his grave — ﴿وَنَحْشُرُهُ﴾ — i.e. the one who turns away from the Quran — ﴿يَوْمَ الْقِيَمَةِ أَعْمَى﴾ — blind of sight.

celaleyn:125-125.t: ﴿قَالَ رَبِّ لِمَ حَشَرْتَنِي أَعْمَى وَقَدْ كُنْتُ بَصِيرًا﴾ — in the world and at the resurrection?

celaleyn:126-126.t: ﴿قَالَ﴾ — the matter is — ﴿كَذَلِكَ أَتَتْكَ آيَاتُنَا فَنَسِيتَهَا﴾ — you abandoned them and did not believe in them — ﴿وَكَذَلِكَ﴾ — like your forgetting Our signs — ﴿الْيَوْمَ تُنْسَى﴾ — you are left in the Fire.

celaleyn:127-127.t: ﴿وَكَذَلِكَ﴾ — and like Our requiting of whoever turns away from the Quran — ﴿نَجْزِي مَنْ أَسْرَفَ﴾ — associated partners with Allah — ﴿وَلَمْ يُؤْمِنْ بِآيَاتِ رَبِّهِ وَلَعَذَابُ الْآخِرَةِ أَشَدُّ﴾ — than the punishment of this world and the punishment of the grave — ﴿وَأَبْقَى﴾ — more lasting.

celaleyn:128-128.t: ﴿أَفَلَمْ يَهْدِ﴾ — has it not become clear — ﴿لَهُمْ﴾ — to the disbelievers of Mecca — ﴿كَمْ﴾ — the declarative (khabariyya) [kam], a mafʿūl (object) — ﴿أَهْلَكْنَا﴾ — i.e. Our destruction of many — ﴿قَبْلَهُمْ مِنَ الْقُرُونِ﴾ — i.e. the past nations, for denying the messengers — ﴿يَمْشُونَ﴾ — a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun of "lahum" — ﴿فِي مَسَاكِنِهِمْ﴾ — on their journeys to Syria and elsewhere, so that they may take heed. And what has been mentioned, namely taking [the maṣdar] "ihlāk" from its verb, which is free of a maṣdar-forming particle, out of regard for the meaning, there is nothing to prevent it. ﴿إِنَّ فِي ذَلِكَ لَآيَاتٍ﴾ — lessons — ﴿لِأُولِي النُّهَى﴾ — for those possessed of intellects.

celaleyn:129-129.t: ﴿وَلَوْلَا كَلِمَةٌ سَبَقَتْ مِنْ رَبِّكَ﴾ — to postpone the punishment from them until the Hereafter — ﴿لَكَانَ﴾ — the destruction — ﴿لِزَامًا﴾ — binding upon them in this world. ﴿وَأَجَلٌ مُسَمًّى﴾ — set for them; conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the latent (mustatir) pronoun in "kāna", and the separation by its khabar (predicate) took the place of the tawkīd (emphasis).

celaleyn:130-130.t: ﴿فَاصْبِرْ عَلَى مَا يَقُولُونَ﴾ — abrogated by the verse of fighting — ﴿وَسَبِّحْ﴾ — pray — ﴿بِحَمْدِ رَبِّكَ﴾ — a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. accompanied by it — ﴿قَبْلَ طُلُوعِ الشَّمْسِ﴾ — the dawn prayer — ﴿وَقَبْلَ غُرُوبِهَا﴾ — the afternoon (ʿaṣr) prayer — ﴿وَمِنْ آنَاءِ اللَّيْلِ﴾ — its hours — ﴿فَسَبِّحْ﴾ — pray the sunset (maghrib) and the night (ʿishāʾ) prayers — ﴿وَأَطْرَافَ النَّهَارِ﴾ — conjoined to the position of "min ānāʾi", which is accusative; i.e. pray the noon (ẓuhr) prayer, because its time begins with the sun's passing the meridian, so it is the end of the first half and the beginning of the second half — ﴿لَعَلَّكَ تَرْضَى﴾ — with the reward you will be given.

celaleyn:131-131.t: ﴿وَلَا تَمُدَّنَّ عَيْنَيْكَ إِلَى مَا مَتَّعْنَا بِهِ أَزْوَاجًا﴾ — kinds — ﴿مِنْهُمْ زَهْرَةَ الْحَيَاةِ الدُّنْيَا﴾ — its adornment and splendour — ﴿لِنَفْتِنَهُمْ فِيهِ﴾ — in that they transgress. ﴿وَرِزْقُ رَبِّكَ﴾ — in Paradise — ﴿خَيْرٌ﴾ — than what they have been given in this world — ﴿وَأَبْقَى﴾ — more lasting.

celaleyn:132-132.t: ﴿وَأْمُرْ أَهْلَكَ بِالصَّلَوةِ وَاصْطَبِرْ﴾ — be patient — ﴿عَلَيْهَا لَا نَسْأَلُكَ﴾ — We do not charge you with — ﴿رِزْقًا﴾ — for yourself or for anyone else. ﴿نَحْنُ نَرْزُقُكَ وَالْعَاقِبَةُ﴾ — Paradise — ﴿لِلتَّقْوَى﴾ — for its people.

celaleyn:133-133.t: ﴿وَقَالُوا﴾ — i.e. the idolaters — ﴿لَوْلَا﴾ — why does not — ﴿يَأْتِينَا﴾ — Muḥammad — ﴿بِآيَةٍ مِنْ رَبِّهِ﴾ — of those they propose? ﴿أَوَلَمْ تَأْتِهِمْ﴾ — with tāʾ and with yāʾ — ﴿بَيِّنَةُ﴾ — the explanation of — ﴿مَا فِي الصُّحُفِ الْأُولَى﴾ — which the Quran contains, of the reports of the past nations and their destruction for denying the messengers?

celaleyn:134-134.t: ﴿وَلَوْ أَنَّا أَهْلَكْنَاهُمْ بِعَذَابٍ مِنْ قَبْلِهِ﴾ — before Muḥammad the Messenger — ﴿لَقَالُوا﴾ — on the Day of Resurrection — ﴿رَبَّنَا لَوْلَا﴾ — why did You not — ﴿أَرْسَلْتَ إِلَيْنَا رَسُولًا فَنَتَّبِعَ آيَاتِكَ﴾ — sent with him — ﴿مِنْ قَبْلِ أَنْ نَذِلَّ﴾ — at the Resurrection — ﴿وَنَخْزَى﴾ — in Hell?

celaleyn:135-135.t: ﴿قُلْ﴾ — to them — ﴿كُلٌّ﴾ — of us and of you — ﴿مُتَرَبِّصٌ﴾ — awaiting how the matter will turn out. ﴿فَتَرَبَّصُوا فَسَتَعْلَمُونَ﴾ — at the Resurrection — ﴿مَنْ أَصْحَابُ الصِّرَاطِ﴾ — the path — ﴿السَّوِيِّ﴾ — the straight — ﴿وَمَنِ اهْتَدَى﴾ — from error: we or you.
